doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Playing lead in Bill's band after Marshall Royal
summary: Nobody should imitate Royal's or Hodges' signature pieces.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: But you know I play lead sometimes with Bill’s band when I can be here now, and I’ve told Bill up front, I wouldn’t try and, you don’t even try to play those things the way Marshall did. It’s a whole different style. He played “Warm Valley” and the thing we’re going to play tonight “Isfa —” It’s a thing written for Johnny Hodges [“Isfahan”]. But all those things that are synonymous with either Johnny Hodges or Marshall, there’s no point in anyone trying to do that. That’s not the way I feel them, and I mean I can get them off reasonably well but it’s still not the same thing. I don’t even remember the question you asked. Oh you asked me about Marshall. He was a great guy. He really was a great guy.
